description: Check whether the final paper establishes a held-out black-box online input flow for the case-specific user task.

note: §4.3 and Fig. 2 disclose task-conditioned strategy generation and failure reasoning during library construction (https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-main.2055.pdf#page=5). §4.5 describes the library as prebuilt offline and describes online context inference from MCP interactions (https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-main.2055.pdf#page=6). Available evidence does not bind the strategy-generation inputs to the held-out black-box online condition. See papers/AdapTools/METHODOLOGY_COMPARISON.md:12–17.
claim: The held-out online black-box constructor receives the current evaluated user task in breach of the final paper’s black-box knowledge restriction.

policy_application.reason: §4.1 excludes current task/state information for the third-party black-box actor. This check is limited to that online arm, rather than the grey-box MCP actor or offline library development.

delivery.reason: §4.3 describes task-conditioned offline development, while §4.5 describes a prebuilt library and online inference. No bound input path ties those development inputs to the current held-out black-box task.

refutation.reason: No positive counterevidence refutes this scoped suspicion.

claim: Using the operator-supplied benign task in offline discovery exceeds MUZZLE’s declared discovery-stage permissions.

policy_application.reason: §§2.3 and 3.1 specifically disclose local discovery and the operator-provided task specification; this is a positive entitlement for the scoped discovery stage.

refutation.reason: The paper specifically authorizes this offline task input. That permission refutes the claim that this disclosed input alone violates the discovery-stage model.

refutation.reason: No positive counterevidence refutes this scoped suspicion.

policy_application.reason: §3.3 allows varying attacker knowledge and §3.4 defines distinct utility and targeted-success outcomes. Those definitions do not bind a particular prohibited private-query flow for the phenomenon in this control.

delivery.reason: No corresponding raw construction request or private-query delivery evidence was supplied for this reported phenomenon.

refutation.reason: Content integrity and task utility concern task completion and outcome interpretation. Those outcomes alone do not establish prohibited information receipt; this refutes only the claimed sufficiency of that inference.

policy_application.reason: §3.2 defines attack goals/capabilities and Table 4 defines outcome metrics. The report of an externally selected action does not by itself bind an applicable private-query prohibition and delivery edge.

refutation.reason: Appendix C.2.3 defines outcome metrics and C.2.5 distinguishes parsing model output and executing simulated tools. note: The attachment’s reported 73.58%→9.25% ASR figures and the alleged forced-action defect remain unverified. This case does not affirm that ASB is otherwise conformant or that its whole information model is problem-free.
